subject: PrivDeploy IaC: cross-tool gating, egress validation and CI artifacts
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Fernando Ruiz <fernando.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: PrivDeploy IaC: cross-tool gating, egress validation and CI artifacts

Hi Fernando —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we prepare the private deployment bundle for your staging VPC, a few gating items came up from our internal compliance and infra teams that I want to align on before we hand off artifacts into your CI:

1) Egress validation: we need a definitive egress policy for the model-serving nodes (allowed destinations + DNS egress). Can you confirm whether outbound to the following is permitted from the subnet where nodes will run?
   - registry.redwood-inference.net (443)
   - update-checks.redwood-inference.net (443)
   - S3 endpoints for artifact fetch (s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com)

2) Artifact signing: we will provide a Terraform module and Helm values with signed provenance. Is Acme able to accept SHA256-signed TF plans and OCI-signed Helm charts, or do you have a signing/trust store we should use?

3) CI/CD gating: we plan to submit a small snippet for your pipeline that runs terraform validate/plan (with planfile) and helm lint + a dry-run. Does your pipeline support a plan artifact upload and verified signature check step? If not, we can adapt.

I'm attaching the initial plan + helm values we intend to deliver for review. If useful, I can loop in our infra lead (Laura) and our architect (Karthik) to walk the team through the bundling approach.

Next steps: if you can confirm the three points above and any pipeline constraints, we'll freeze the artifact formats and gate the delivery.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: priv-iac-plan.tf (Terraform plan stub), helm-values-acme.yaml (Helm values), ci-pipeline-snippet.yml (CI snippet)
From: Fernando Ruiz <fernando.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-team@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: cross-tool gating, egress validation and CI artifacts

Ben —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers from the Acme infra team:

1) Egress: outbound to the three destinations you listed is fine. Our security policy requires that you also provide a CIDR allowlist when possible (we'll bind it into an egress security group). For DNS, we prefer using our internal resolver; outgoing DNS to 8.8.8.8 is blocked.

2) Artifact signing: we accept SHA256-signed artifacts and have an internal key registry. Can you publish Helm charts to our internal OCI registry (oci.acme-corp.com) and sign with an OCI signature? We'll send a short key exchange process.

3) CI gating: our pipeline (AcmeCI) supports artifact uploads and signature checks. However, to integrate your plan verification step we need a small wrapper that:
   - stores planfile as an artifact
   - triggers a downstream verification job that checks signature + tfplan contents against a whitelist of allowed resources

I'll loop in procurement to confirm the timeline for key exchange. I'll add Laura and Karthik to the thread so we can align on the signature/plan format and any constraints in the TF modules.

-- Fernando
Fernando Ruiz
Head of Cloud Platform, Acme Corp
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Fernando Ruiz <fernando.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: cross-tool gating, egress validation and CI artifacts

Fernando — thanks for the quick clarifications. 

Laura / Karthik — tagging you both because Acme asked for the exact artifact shapes and a plan for key exchange + pipeline wrapper. High level asks from Acme that will drive how we package:

- Provide TF planfiles plus a signed artifact (SHA256) and an accompanying provenance file (we propose simple JSON with plan hash, module versions, and build job id).
- Publish Helm charts to their OCI registry and sign them; also include the values file as a signed blob.
- Supply a CI wrapper script (POSIX shell) that: uploads the planfile to AcmeCI, invokes their verifier job, and returns non-zero on mismatch. We'll attach a candidate snippet.

Questions for you both:
1) The Terraform module currently uses a few data sources that resolve internal AZ ranges and route tables at plan time; Acme wants a whitelist of allowed resource types — can we add a pre-flight check to our module to emit a resource-usage manifest (list of resource types and counts) as part of plan generation?
2) For Helm, we currently template the egress rules into values at package time. Would it be safe to include both an explicit host allowlist and an annotation that signals "use-acme-resolver" (so the cluster's CNI can rewrite DNS)?
3) For key exchange, do we draft a short runbook that their security team can follow to add our signing key to their registry trust store? I can draft that.

I've attached the pipeline snippet and the current plan stub for your review (they're the same attachments Ben sent yesterday but with module comments). If you prefer a short call to walk the approach we can book 30 minutes Thu or Fri.

Thanks —
Ben

Attachments: priv-iac-plan.tf (annotated), ci-pipeline-snippet.yml
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Fernando Ruiz <fernando.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: cross-tool gating, egress validation and CI artifacts

Fernando / team —

We're aligned on the gating approach. A few action items from Redwood's side:

- Karthik will add a pre-flight resource manifest generator to the Terraform module (outputs a small JSON printed to stdout and stored as planfile metadata). This addresses the whitelist ask.
- We'll produce signed planfiles (sha256) and a provenance JSON that includes module versions, provider checksums, and pipeline job id. Example provenance schema will be uploaded to the Drive link below.
- For Helm, we'll produce both: a values file with explicit egress allowlist and a small annotation (redwood.io/use-acme-resolver: "true"). We'll leave DNS behavior to Acme's CNI.
- I'll draft the key-exchange runbook and the short wrapper script for AcmeCI; Ben will send the draft by end of day Monday.

Please confirm any additional constraints on resource types we should include in the whitelist (e.g., block creation of public IPs, restrict IAM roles). If you can sign the key exchange doc once we share it, we can proceed to create signed artifacts and a validation job in your pipeline.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PrivDeployArtifacts
Jira: INFRA-1427

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: helm-values-acme.yaml (proposed values), priv-iac-plan.tf (annotated), ci-pipeline-snippet.yml (wrapper)
